note:
How fine must the optics be? Spot minimum swept 1-100 um on the 34-core die at density 1.60.
The array achieves the SAME thermal result at every spot size -- identical heat removed, peak
and throughput. What changes is the electrical COST, because a spot larger than its target
block must be diluted over silicon that did not need cooling.
THE_REQUIREMENT_IS_50_UM_NOT_10: Cost is flat within 3 % from 1 um to 50 um and jumps 20 % at 100 um (68.1 -> 82.0 W for the same 112.5 W lifted). So the optics requirement is a spot at or below ~50 um, which is FIVE TIMES looser than the 10 um this project has been assuming. Going finer than 50 um buys nothing measurable.
AND_THE_FLOORPLAN_EXPLAINS_WHY: The median block min-dimension on this die is 45.4 um and 714 of 1126 blocks are narrower than 100 um. A spot larger than its target block wastes light on neighbours that did not need it, so the knee sits where the spot starts exceeding typical block width -- between 50 and 100 um, exactly as measured. The requirement is therefore set by the FLOORPLAN, not by the device: a die with coarser blocks would tolerate a coarser spot.
WHAT_THIS_IS_NOT: Not a claim that spot size is free. It is a claim that below ~50 um the constraint stops binding ON THIS FLOORPLAN at this density. The thermal result was identical at every point, so this measures cost, not capability, and a shape with finer hot blocks would move the knee.
